faq.q: What is the National Pension System (NPS)?
faq.a: NPS is a voluntary, long-term retirement savings scheme regulated by the PFRDA. It aims to provide old-age income security to Indian citizens, allowing them to build a retirement corpus through market-linked returns.

faq.q: How does Aditya Birla Sun Life Pension Fund manage my NPS money?
faq.a: Aditya Birla Sun Life Pension Fund, like other PFMs, invests your contributions across different asset classes – Equity (E), Corporate Bonds (C), and Government Securities (G) – based on your chosen allocation (Active Choice) or an age-based automatic allocation (Auto Choice).

faq.q: Can I change my Pension Fund Manager (PFM)?
faq.a: Yes, NPS subscribers have the flexibility to change their Pension Fund Manager (PFM) once in a financial year. This can be done online through your CRA account.

faq.q: What are the tax benefits of investing in NPS?
faq.a: NPS offers significant tax benefits under Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakhs), Section 80CCD(1B) (additional deduction of ₹50,000 for NPS contributions), and tax exemption on 60% of the corpus withdrawn at retirement.

faq.q: Is NPS suitable for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)?
faq.a: Yes, NRIs are eligible to open an NPS account. They can contribute to NPS using funds from their NRE/NRO accounts, subject to FEMA regulations.

NPS returns are market-linked and depend on the performance of the underlying assets (equities, corporate bonds, government securities) managed by your chosen PFM. Returns are expressed as Net Asset Value (NAV) growth over time.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS corpus upon retirement?
faq.a: At retirement (age 60), you can withdraw up to 60% of your accumulated corpus as a lump sum (which is tax-exempt). The remaining minimum 40% must be used to purchase an annuity plan from an IRDAI-regulated life insurance company, which provides a regular pension.
